answer: Each identity claims one ferrous plate, locks a 75-credit bond, and gets a forge-stamped serial. Each epoch the owner files a pulse-echo reading, the return time of a pulse through it. An auditor recomputes thickness from the ferrous echo-time table; a 3% miss, reused serial, or two keys on one plate burns the bond. First filing costs 40, the k-th 40+6(k-1): the 1000th 6034; 1000 fakes pay 3,037,000 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-plate ring fails: one serial binds one plate to one key, and its echo fits no other. An honest agent pays 40 once and locks 75 once, refunded after a clean epoch.
